transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Acme ML - ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Acme ML - Product), Liam O'Neill (Acme ML - Infra)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics, tokens/sec/$, observed caching savings so far, and batching tradeoffs. Agreed to rerun a couple simulations and share updated benchmark sheet.

Topics: cost/k, caching impact, batching vs latency, Dedicated vs Hosted TCO, next steps for pilot scale.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're at 10:00 so we'll kick off. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya: hi priya here, hey.
[00:08] Carlos: carlos on product.
[00:10] Liam: liam infra.
[00:12] Maya: maya from redwood, samir here as well.
[00:15] Jordan: cool, quick agenda, recap last week's changes to caching, batching runs, and then dig into tokens per dollar numbers you asked for.
[00:23] Priya: yep that's what we care about, especially the tokens per dollar with our 95th pctl latency SLO, we can't trade cost for latency past a point.
[00:30] Maya: totally, and we have the updated benchmark sheet in the shared drive - link in the invite - but i'll summarize key numbers.
[00:36] Maya: so baseline hosted run (open model v-2 quantized) without prefix cache, batch size 1: about 120 tokens/sec on a single GPU and cost per 1k tokens around $0.095.
[00:50] Carlos: quick question — those numbers are at ~256 seq length?
[00:53] Maya: yes average response length in these tests is 220 tokens, input prefixes average 30 tokens.
[00:58] Jordan: and important bit: when we enable prefix/KV caching for warm users we see tokens/sec improvements and cost drop.
[01:05] Priya: what was the cache hit rate you used?
[01:08] Maya: in the first run we used a modest 40% hit rate, that's reflective of your observed repeat prompts. with 40% hit and cache served from memory the effective tokens/sec jumps to ~170 and cost/1k drops to about $0.06, roughly 35-40% savings.
[01:26] Liam: that 40% number matches our internal trace for week 1 after dedup but curious what happens if hit rate is lower, like 20%.
[01:33] Maya: at 20% hit it's more modest, tokens/sec around 140 and cost/1k roughly $0.08. also batching plays in — if you increase batch size you can amortize kernel overhead but latency goes up.
[01:44] Priya: can you quantify latency impact? we need 95th pctl under 300ms for interactive UI.
[01:50] Maya: with batch size 4 on the same setup tail latency moved from ~180ms to ~350-400ms, so that violates 95th pctl. batch size 2 gave a 10-15% throughput gain with tail still within SLO.
[02:03] Jordan: so practically for Acme's SLO, batch=2 + prefix cache ~40% is sweet spot. cost-wise that gives about 30% reduction from baseline.
[02:13] Carlos: ok that's promising. what about reserved capacity or Dedicated? the dev team asked if Dedicated would be cheaper at scale.
[02:20] Maya: good point — Dedicated reduces unit GPU rental overhead and you can tune instance types. in our rough TCO model, if you sustain >2M tokens/day with steady throughput, Dedicated starts to look 15-25% cheaper after accounting for reserved capacity discounts and improved batch packing.
[02:35] Priya: do those numbers include ops overhead and the cost of additional cache memory?
[02:38] Maya: yes we included a small uplift for memory and management, but not network egress. if you plan on VPC/private deploy there are networking costs to add.
[02:45] Liam: on-prem considerations — our infra team flagged egress policies and hardware allocation windows, but capacity is available for the pilot window. need to confirm GPU availability for Dedicated.
[02:56] Jordan: noted, liam to follow up on GPU slots and expected up/down windows.
[03:00] Liam: yep will check.
[03:02] Maya: back to numbers — here's a couple more caveats: quantization level affects throughput too; int8 gives better perf but sometimes small perplexity increases; we ran int8 and q4 we saw 10-20% perf diffs.
[03:15] Priya: did you observe any quality regressions with q4?
[03:18] Maya: minimal on your eval set; a couple edge cases around numerical extraction but overall pass rate was 96% on the eval prompts you shared.
[03:27] Carlos: good. any thoughts on multi-model routing? some of our flows can use a smaller model for short replies and large model for long ones.
[03:34] Maya: absolutely — smart routing reduces cost by routing short prompts to a smaller model (tokens/sec higher, lower cost) and long form to the larger model. caching still applies per model route. in simulation mixed routing gave ~28% cost savings compared to single-model no-routing baseline.
[03:50] Priya: can you show the numbers in the benchmark sheet?
[03:53] Maya: yes it's in the sheet with columns for hit rate, batch size, model variant, tokens/sec, cost/1k, tail latency.
[03:59] Jordan: let's walk one of the rows live — Maya can you share your screen?
[04:05] Maya: i can, connecting...
[04:28] Maya: all right sharing. so this row here is baseline no-cache, batch1, 120 tok/s, $0.095/1k. then this row shows cache40% batch2, 165 tok/s, $0.064/1k.
[04:46] Carlos: where are you factoring in cache memory cost?
[04:49] Maya: we amortize cache memory across requests and it's a small delta — we modeled about $0.005/1k tokens as cache overhead in worst case.
[04:58] Priya: so net saving still ~30%?
[05:01] Maya: yes net-ish 28-32% depending on hit.
[05:05] Samir: quick operational note — warm-up behavior matters, first warm-up window has lower hit rates. recommended to pre-warm with top 500 prefixes if you have stable users.
[05:15] Priya: we do have about 200 power users that account for 40% of traffic, so pre-warming could help.
[05:21] Maya: exactly — that maps to your 40% hit scenario well.
[05:24] Priya: any concerns on skewed request patterns causing cache thrash?
[05:28] Maya: possibility if you have highly diverse prompts; eviction policy matters. we can tune LRU vs LFU; we tested an LFU-sim and it improved hit for your distribution slightly.
[05:37] Liam: on batching tradeoffs, curious about dynamic batching thresholds — can Redwood tune thresholds so that batch grows only when latency is safe?
[05:45] Maya: yes we have workload-aware batching — thresholding and deadlines so that we avoid increasing tail latency beyond SLO. the runtime can be configured per-route.
[05:53] Carlos: you mentioned tokens/sec per dollar earlier — can you walk through the math quickly?
[05:57] Jordan: sure quick math: tokens/sec is throughput; cost per 1k tokens is (GPU cost per sec / tok/sec) * 1000 plus amortized infra. so increasing tok/sec via cache or batching lowers cost/1k.
[06:09] Priya: can you give an example with numbers?
[06:11] Jordan: baseline GPU rental = $X per hour, convert to $/sec, divide by tok/sec 120, gives base, then add infra overhead. Maya's sheet has exact constants.
[06:19] Carlos: is the GPU cost the hosted rate or market GPU price?
[06:23] Maya: for hosted we use our internal hosted rate; for Dedicated we use reserved cost model with discount assumptions. both are in the sheet.
[06:30] Priya: another question — how does prefix caching interact with function calling or tool calling in our flows? sometimes calls trigger additional tokens server side.
[06:38] Maya: function calls increase overall token count; caching helps prefilled prefix tokens but not the tool-call generated tokens. so cost savings apply mostly to the repeated prefix parts. for tool-heavy flows you still get some benefit but less proportional.
[06:50] Carlos: did you run an experiment with a 50% cache hit scenario?
[06:53] Maya: yes 50% hit bumped tokens/sec to ~180 and cost to ~$0.055/1k. down side: cache memory needs scale linearly with hit targets.
[07:05] Liam: what's the advice on cache sizing for Acme's dataset?
[07:08] Maya: pre-warm top 500 prefixes and allocate 4GB of cache for the pilot; that got us to ~45-50% hit in simulation.
[07:17] Priya: 4GB ok, but need to check infra approvals.
[07:20] Liam: i'll check.
[07:22] Samir: small note on billing granularity — hosted billed per token, dedicated often billed per reserved capacity; we'll produce an apples-to-apples TCO in the sheet.
[07:32] Jordan: moving on to tail latency mitigation — we recommend concurrency limits per instance and route-based SLO failovers to lower-cost model or traffic shaping to keep pctl in line.
[07:44] Priya: what about graceful degradation? can Redwood automatically fallback to a smaller model when latency spikes?
[07:50] Maya: yes we support routing policies and automatic fallback to smaller model variants; you can set latency thresholds to trigger that. we can demo failover behavior in the next deep-dive.
[08:00] Carlos: let's flag that as a follow-up.
[08:02] Jordan: noted. next, security/compliance impacts on cost — Priya you asked last week about audit logging retention cost?
[08:10] Priya: yeah, how much extra does 90-day audit log retention add?
[08:14] Samir: rough estimate is +$0.01/1k tokens depending on log verbosity and retention; again we can narrow that in the security doc.
[08:24] Priya: acceptable for now.
[08:27] Maya: quick question for you — do you expect traffic to increase week over week during pilot?
[08:31] Priya: we expect ramp by ~30% starting week 2 because of additional internal users.
[08:36] Maya: ok that changes TCO projections; we'll rerun the simulation with +30% traffic.
[08:41] Jordan: moving into the simulation results we ran this morning — Maya, can you show the mixed routing + cache + batch2 row?
[08:47] Maya: yes this row shows mixed routing (small model for <40 char replies), cache 45%, batch2, tokens/sec effective 210, cost/1k $0.048, taillatency 220ms.
[09:01] Carlos: 210 tokens/sec seems high — are we counting combined across models?
[09:05] Maya: yes effective tokens/sec weighted across routes; smaller model responses are much cheaper per token which helps the average.
[09:12] Priya: are there any quality tradeoffs using smaller model for short replies?
[09:15] Maya: mostly fine for template responses; for creative or nuance heavy replies use bigger model. route rules can be content or token-length based.
[09:23] Liam: from infra side, if we route to two models we need capacity for both; does Redwood autoscale independently per model?
[09:29] Maya: yes autoscale per model pool and we support overprovision/burst policies.
[09:34] Jordan: ok moving toward decisions, we need to pick a pilot config for next week: hosted vs Dedicated, cache size, batch target. thoughts?
[09:44] Priya: we'd like to start hosted to move fast, but we want a clear path to Dedicated if costs look better; hosted pilot with cache prewarm top 500 and batch2 sounds reasonable.
[09:54] Carlos: agree start hosted, run 1-week smoke and then evaluate Dedicated TCO mid-pilot.
[09:59] Maya: will set batch default to 2, prewarm script to top 500 prefixes, enable LFU eviction.
[10:07] Liam: i'll verify network and egress constraints; if there's any issue we'll pause prewarm.
[10:12] Samir: i'll share the SSO + security doc pack after this call.
[10:16] Jordan: excellent. now quick risks and mitigation: risk of cache not hitting due to prompt variability -> mitigate with pre-warm and route tuning. risk of latency SLO misses with batch>2 -> mitigate with dynamic batching and failover.
[10:29] Priya: agree those look good.
[10:31] Jordan: to recap action items...
[10:33] Jordan: Maya rerun caching sim with +10% cache and report [due 3/14]. Jordan send Dedicated pricing and TCO [3/14]. Priya share prompts/traces [3/15]. Liam confirm GPU windows [3/18]. Samir send security pack [3/14].
[10:49] Carlos: fine.
[10:51] Priya: thanks all.
[10:53] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in calendar.
[10:56] End of meeting.
